QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_17

question.text: Ms. Priya Shah (SIA) is designing the assessment methodology for Kiran Healthcare Pvt Ltd's cataract-surgery program. Of the following, which technique provides the STRONGEST causal inference about whether improved vision is due to the intervention?

answer.text: Pre-post comparison of the treated group only
Randomised Controlled Trial (RCT) with a randomly assigned control group
Narrative testimonials from ten satisfied beneficiaries

explanation.text: The Logic: In impact evaluation methodology generally, a Randomised Controlled Trial (RCT) with a randomly assigned control group provides the strongest causal inference because random assignment makes the treatment and control groups statistically equivalent on observable and unobservable characteristics, so any post-intervention difference can be attributed to the intervention rather than to selection or secular trends. The Trap: Pre-post comparison of only the treated group cannot rule out time trends or external influences. Management self-assessment via structured questionnaire is subject to self-reporting bias and has no counterfactual. Narrative testimonials from a few satisfied beneficiaries are anecdotal and suffer from selection bias. Note: The "RCT as strongest causal-inference technique" hierarchy is general impact-evaluation knowledge and is not explicitly stated in the Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026), which focuses on evidence, sampling, Theory of Change, SIA approaches, and evaluation models. The reasoning above reflects standard industry practice in evaluation research.
